title: Expected Value Reasoning

body_head: # Expected Value Reasoning  ## Summary Expected value reasoning multiplies each outcome's value by its probability and sums, choosing the highest total. title: Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
description: The claim that sparse subnetworks can match full networks
body_head: # Lottery Ticket Hypothesis  ## Summary The lottery ticket hypothesis claims dense networks contain sparse subnetworks ('winning tickets') that can train alone to match full-network accuracy. Frankle and Carbin's original finding was striking: train a network, prune the smallest-magnitude weights, reset the survivors to their initial training values, retrain — and the small pruned network reaches the original's accuracy, often faster. The dense network was hiding a sparse one that was already poised to learn.  ## Details - The procedure is iterative magnitude pruning with rewinding: train, prune, rewind surviving weights to an earlier training point (originally initialization), and retrain

title: Means-Ends Analysis
description: Reducing the difference between current state and goal step by step
body_head: # Means-Ends Analysis  ## Summary Means-ends analysis plans by measuring the difference between the current state and the goal, then choosing actions that reduce the largest difference, recursively handling subproblems. Modern LLM planners echo it when they decompose obstacles.  ## Details - Loop: detect salient difference → find operator that reduces it → apply → recurse. body_head: # Metacircular Evaluators  ## Summary A metacircular evaluator is an interpreter written in the language it interprets — most famously the Lisp evaluator 'eval' defined in Lisp, canonicalized in SICP. body_head: # Perception Loop  ## Summary The perception loop is the front end of the agent cycle: raw events and tool outputs are parsed, filtered, and turned into structured state that reasoning can use. description: Treating planning as a search problem over states and actions
body_head: # Planning as Search  ## Summary Planning as search frames planning as searching a state space: nodes are states, edges are actions, and the plan is the path to a goal state. It matters because it imports the whole toolkit of search algorithms — BFS, A*, iterative deepening — into planning. It is the classical backbone of planning systems.  ## Details - The mapping is direct: the initial state is the start node, goal states are target nodes, each action is an edge to a successor state, and a plan is a path from start to goal. title: Policy Gradient
description: Learning policies directly by gradient ascent on expected reward
body_head: # Policy Gradient  ## Summary Policy gradient methods optimize the policy directly: estimate the gradient of expected reward with respect to policy parameters and ascend it. title: Proactionary Principle
description: Favoring innovation and risk-taking unless harm is demonstrated
body_head: # Proactionary Principle  ## Summary The proactionary principle favors proceeding with innovation absent demonstrated severe harm, prioritizing opportunity cost. Where the precautionary principle says "do not proceed until safety is established", the proactionary principle says "do not block progress until harm is demonstrated" — the burden of proof sits on those who would restrict, and the cost of missed opportunity is counted as a real cost.  ## Details - The logic is consequentialist: innovation produces benefits — cures, capabilities, economic growth — and preventing it has costs that are just as real as the harms it might avoid. title: Probabilistic Inference
description: Drawing conclusions about unknowns from data under uncertainty
body_head: # Probabilistic Inference  ## Summary  Probabilistic Inference — Drawing conclusions about unknowns from data under uncertainty.  ## Details  - Probabilistic inference computes what is reasonable to believe about unknowns given observed data and an explicit model of uncertainty. Two traditions coexist: frequentist inference (long-run error rates, p-values, confidence intervals) and Bayesian inference (posterior distributions over parameters). - Both rely on the same probability calculus; they differ in what 'probability' means and what claims are licensed. Key instruments: likelihood functions, estimation, hypothesis testing, and prediction — with model checking as the constant companion.

body_head: # Probing Classifiers  ## Summary Probing classifiers are small models trained on a model's internal activations to test whether features are linearly accessible. title: Procedural Memory

body_head: # Procedural Memory  ## Summary Procedural memory encodes how to perform tasks: sequences, tool habits, and skills that no longer need deliberation. It matters because compiled procedures are what make agents fast and consistent. For RSIS3, L2 prompt and code tuning is procedural learning.  ## Details - Differs from declarative memory: knowing how, not knowing that. - Grows through repetition and successful execution. - In agents: cached strategies, prompt templates, and refined tool call patterns. - Open questions: how to version and review learned procedures safely. - Procedural memory stores how to do things — skills and routines — acquired through practice and expressed as performance

title: Production Rules

body_head: # Production Rules  ## Summary Production rules are IF condition THEN action rules evaluated against working memory; when a condition matches, the action fires, possibly changing state and enabling other rules. They matter because they model reactive, modular behavior and are the substrate of classic expert systems. They are also how agents can encode policies.  ## Details - The structure is simple and powerful: each rule is an independent unit — "IF the temperature exceeds 90 AND the device is idle THEN shut it down" — and the system's behavior emerges from the interactions of many such units firing as their conditions become true. title: Publication Bias

body_head: # Publication Bias  ## Summary  Publication bias is the systematic tendency for studies with significant, positive, or novel results to be published while null or negative results languish unpublished. It matters because the published literature then overstates effect sizes, distorting meta-analyses and evidence-based practice. The bias is a property of the publication system, not of any individual study.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Publication decisions correlate with the direction and significance of results, so the visible literature is a biased sample of all research. - **Mechanisms** — Author self-censoring, reviewer and editor preferences, and incentives to publish positive findi

title: Puffery
description: Exaggerated praise that inflates a subject
body_head: # Puffery  ## Summary  Puffery is exaggerated or subjective praise — claims like best, revolutionary, or unmatched — that inflates a subject without verifiable specifics. It matters because puffery erodes trust, misleads readers, and is often legally tolerated while being ethically dubious. In technical and encyclopedic writing, puffery is a quality defect to be stripped in favor of verifiable claims.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Puffery consists of subjective superlatives and vague enthusiasm that cannot be confirmed or falsified. - **Where it appears** — Marketing copy, product pages, resumes, and even documentation drift into puffery when writers substitute enthusiasm for evidence. -

title: Superforecasters
description: Individuals who consistently outperform in probability forecasting
body_head: # Superforecasters  ## Summary  Superforecasters are people who consistently produce more accurate probability forecasts than experts and the general public, as documented in long-running forecasting tournaments. They matter because their habits are trainable and transferable: decomposing problems, updating on evidence, and tracking calibration. Their existence shows that judgment skill is real, measurable, and improvable.  ## Details  - **Definition** — The label emerged from forecasting tournaments where a small set of participants repeatedly beat benchmarks, domain experts, and aggregated forecasts. - **Habits** — They break questions into components, seek base rates, update frequently

title: Superposition Research
description: Studying how networks pack many features into few dimensions
body_head: # Superposition Research  ## Summary Superposition research studies how neural networks store more features than dimensions, exploiting sparsity and correlation structure.
